claims.text: The seed is the first post of a four-part thread by Odysseus (@odysseas_eth), founder of Phylax Systems, posted 2026-10-29 at 20:54 UTC.
The thread was drawn to 235,011 views within hours.

The sweep transaction, `0x53bd38b8…e2f3`, is in block 26300770 with timestamp 2026-10-29 20:24:23 UTC and shows an internal transfer of 167,464.2478 ETH plus 63 ERC-20 transfers from Binance 14 to an address Etherscan labels "Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter 2".
The largest legs were roughly 1.615 billion USDT, 62.6 million RLUSD, 29,934 wBETH, 11,372 XAUt, 6.19 million UNI and 198 million ENA.
The delegation transaction, `0xad99264d…`, sits in block 26300753 at 20:20:59 UTC and is a type-4 (EIP-7702) transaction carrying 50 authorizations.

On-chain, the sweep was a plain type-2 transaction sent by the attacker's externally owned account, `0x7C86…5CA0`, at sender nonce 11, calling `sweep()` on Binance 14; it carried no authorization list.
The delegation transaction was sent by that same account at nonce 10.
The attacker paid the gas for both, about 0.0065 ETH for the delegation and under a thousandth of an ETH for the sweep, so the victim wallet needed no ETH to be emptied.
Binance 14 was busy, sending 33 transactions in the three minutes before the attack, about one every six seconds.
The carrying transaction held 50 authorizations for nonces 18,914,775 through 18,914,824; the wallet's nonce reached 18,914,808 by inclusion, and only the authorization for 18,914,809 was valid.

Etherscan shows verified source, a contract named "Target" compiled with Solidity 0.8.28, exposing `sweep(to, tokens[])`, `callExecute(target, to, value, data)`, `withdrawETH` and `withdrawToken`, and the bytecode hard-codes the attacker's operator address as the only authorized caller.
Early press and Blockaid called the contract unverified; the Etherscan page now shows it verified, a discrepancy best explained by verification after the fact, though that is inference.
Blockaid found it still active at 22:00 UTC, 808bits at 23:50, and a second sweep of Binance 14 took about 200 million USDT at 21:44.
Binance cleared it at 00:10:35 UTC on 30 October with an authorization to the zero address
Nine transactions deploy a sweeper and delegate throwaway accounts using 2- and 3-nonce windows.

Binance's account, published 2026-10-30 at 02:23, is that its initial probe "may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop," giving access to a service container used to submit unauthorized withdrawals, and that it has "found no evidence of any wallet private key leak."
Blockaid's wording is stronger: a copy of the Binance 14 key signed the authorizations.
Its chief executive later said the pattern looked like a compromise of signing infrastructure rather than a leaked key.

What the chain does show is breadth: ten other Binance hot wallets were drained with ordinary transactions signed by their own keys across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Bitcoin, Tron and more.
The $2.8 billion figure is Etherscan data for Ethereum alone.
Blockaid's "at least $5.5 billion" rests on public tallies across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Bitcoin and Tron.
Arkham's tally, relayed by ChainCatcher, is $6.01 billion across nine chains.
TRM puts gross theft at about $6.36 billion across ten chains at theft-time prices, or $6.23 billion at later prices.
On Ethereum, TRM counts 200,630 ETH plus 185 tokens including 1.875 billion USDT, 823 million USDC and 88.5 million RLUSD
18,270 BTC left on the Bitcoin chain in eleven transactions in one block around 20:20 UTC

Tether froze about 1.77 billion USDT, Circle about 825 million USDC, Ripple 40.5 million RLUSD, and World Liberty Financial 27.8 million USD1, while the Arbitrum Security Council moved 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB (about $30 million) to a restricted wallet.
Tether's first freeze, 971.1 million USDT at the main receiving wallet, came at 21:01 UTC, 37 minutes after the sweep, and Circle's followed at 21:04.
Executives' own numbers were lower early: Tether's chief executive said more than $1.567 billion and Circle's said more than $800 million.
Independent on-chain work by CryptoTicker found 1.1755 billion USDT and 823 million USDC sitting frozen at the main receiving address, and about 700 million USDT that moved before the freeze.
TRM says the attacker sold about 325 million USDT to market makers at a discount of more than 10%, and deposited 60 million USDT in Aave to borrow about 19,760 ETH.
It reports the attacker holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion, "beyond any issuer's reach,"
TRM attributes the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group "with high confidence,"
Chainalysis's chief executive called it "likely" the same group in CoinDesk, and ZachXBT said likely Lazarus.
An anonymous source in the same CoinDesk piece cautioned there was no definitive attribution and that DPRK groups usually move funds faster.

Sygnia's forensic report traced Bybit to a compromised Safe developer workstation on 4 February 2025, access inside Safe's AWS between 5 and 17 February, a modified S3 script on 19 February and the theft on 21 February
The FBI attributed the roughly $1.5 billion Bybit theft to North Korea within five days.
Chainalysis counted $2.02 billion stolen by DPRK-linked actors in 2025, about 59% of more than $3.4 billion stolen that year.
Binance's SAFU fund was converted to 15,000 BTC in February 2026, worth about $1.0 billion then, with a pledge to top up if it fell below $800 million.
At a Bitcoin price near $79,400 on 29 October the fund was worth about $1.19 billion.
One analyst estimate sets customer assets near $129.4 billion and reserves near $166 billion, and a net gap after freezes and SAFU of about $2.14 billion
Withdrawals", def: "Suspended; Binance's Yi He said resumption was expected within 48 hours
BNB fell 8.6% to about $694 and Korea's KOSPI closed down 4.9%, but a same-day tech and AI-capex selloff led by weak Amazon and Intel results overlapped.
Contemporaneous reporting shows ETH slipping from $2,335 to $2,255 and BTC from $80.8k to $78.8k by 20:51 UTC, and one analyst blamed technology stocks, not the incident.
Liquidations reached $627.7 million within an hour, $606.6 million of them longs and $344.8 million on Binance, the most hack-specific signal.
Taylor Monahan said "It's not actually a 7702 issue," and a Base engineer said the wallets were not hacked using 7702 but already had leaked keys.
SlowMist's Yu Xian said the attacker chose 7702 solely for the convenience of cleanup.
Wintermute reported in June 2025 that more than 90% of delegations it saw were going to malicious sweeper code, a figure The Block reported as more than 80%
EIP-7702, live since the Pectra upgrade of 2025-05-07, lets an externally owned account set its code to a delegation indicator, `0xef0100` followed by an address
Blockaid's detector fired 1 minute 55 seconds after the sweep, while the delegation sat on-chain for 3 minutes 24 seconds before it
Arkham's holdings snapshot lists about $5.875 billion across 65 tokens at a point when the ETH figures conflict across sources (195,460; 420,000; 460,568 ETH).
Its fourth says the delegated wallet used its owner role on a separate smart wallet to move another 780 million USDC at 20:41:23.
